# `for … else` in an imperative body. The else case is "the body never ran",
# which passForElse states as a flag set by the body's first statement and
# tested after the loop -- three statements every backend already emits, so no
# language grows a case for the construct.
#
# Before that pass the generic per-language statement path read a loop's head
# and body and nothing else, and this else block was silently dropped from the
# generated code in all three languages while the interpreter honoured it.

sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --out=go app.sngl
exists go/model.go

grep '__ran0 := false' go/model.go
grep 'if !__ran0 \{' go/model.go
# The flag is set first in the body, so a `continue` cannot skip it.
grep -count=1 '__ran0 = true' go/model.go

# Two loops in one body get a flag each rather than sharing one.
grep '__ran1 := false' go/model.go
grep 'if !__ran1 \{' go/model.go

sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=web app.sngl
grep 'let __ran0 = false;' web/index.html
grep 'if \(!__ran0\) \{' web/index.html

sngl generate --platform=android --lang=kotlin --out=droid app.sngl
grep 'var __ran0 = false' droid/MainScreen.kt
grep 'if \(!__ran0\) \{' droid/MainScreen.kt

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

component main {
    var xs list<int> = []
    var note = ""
    var total = 0

    button(text="run", @click {
        for var x = xs {
            if x == 0 {
                continue
            }
            total = total + x
        } else {
            note = "empty"
        }
        for var y = xs {
            total = total + y
        } else {
            note = "still empty"
        }
    })
    text(value=note)
}
